Provisional income is $222,895, so 85% of Social Security ($41,395) is taxable. AGI is $222,895. The $12,000 senior deduction is reduced by 6% of the $72,895 excess over $150,000, leaving $7,626. After the $32,200 standard deduction and $3,300 age add-on, taxable income is $179,769. Tax under the 2026 joint brackets is $17,393; no NIIT applies.

The conversion increases taxable income and also phases down the senior deduction; the tax increment must be combined with the annual 2028 Part B IRMAA tier increase. On these facts, the conversion moves MAGI into higher IRMAA brackets, adding a full-year premium increase as well as federal tax.

AGE55 applies because the client left in/after the year they turned 55 and plans withdrawals before 59½; the plan exception may avoid the 10% penalty. NUA applies because rolling the low-basis employer stock into an IRA gives up that treatment. COST applies because 1.25% in the IRA exceeds 0.04% in the plan.
ANSWER: AGE55, NUA, COST

Provisional income is $50,050. The worksheet yields 85% of the $16,050 excess over $34,000, plus the lesser of $4,500 or half of benefits: $18,142.50, rounded to $18,143.
ANSWER: 18143
